newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Israelis and Palestinians agree to meet again.
newsitem.headline: Israelis and Palestinians agree to meet again.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian leaders on Tuesday offered hope for the stalled Middle East peace talks, saying they were prepared to meet again to try to restart stalled negotiations.

Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy told European Union intermediaries they were determined direct talks should resume, although they gave no indication when this might happen.

"No timetable has been set for a next meeting, but I can assure you that both sides made a political and moral commitment to meet again and resume talks," said Jacques Poos, the foreign minister of Luxembourg, which holds the current EU presidency.
"They also agreed that the committees (formed by Israel and the Palestinians to negotiate the finer details of the peace process) would get back to work soon," he added.
The breakthrough was hailed by Luxembourg as a feather in the EU's cap in its bid to win a greater say in the Middle East peace process.

The EU convinced Arafat and Levy to meet briefly in April, two months after peace talks broke down. That discussion -- held in Malta on the fringe of another EU meeting -- was marked by terse exchanges and there was no formal joint public appearance.
Tuesday's meeting appeared far more cordial as Arafat and Levy shared a podium with Poos at a news conference.
"I am highly satisfied with our discussions," Levy said. "I am sure we are now going to be able to establish the confidence necessary to proceed."
Arafat agreed. "Significant and positive steps have been taken," he said. "We have to continue these meetings, especially as the peace process is facing serious problems."
Arafat referred to Levy as "our cousin", adding: "I am firmly convinced that he sets great store by the peace process."
Levy said: "I am very satisfied with what I heard in the message from President Arafat."
The meeting, which lasted nearly an hour, was the highest-level contact between Israel and the Palestinians since April.
"The whole system is no longer blocked," Poos said. "The atmosphere was excellent... We discussed ways in which the two parties might restart a dialogue."
Neither Arafat or Levy would elaborate on what had been decided, but both said the meeting was a breakthrough.
Poos later said they had agreed to resume work on the minor committees, a point he described as significant.
Levy earlier gave a spirited defence of Israel's commitment to Middle East peace as he addressed members of the European Parliament's foreign affairs committee in a mixture of French and Hebrew.

"We see peace as a value and a goal, but it is a complicated issue," he said. "I know that some of you feel Israel is not helping the peace process, but this is not us being stubborn, this is us defending out lives."
Levy was given a hostile reception, but retorted to one heckler: "You have to be in Israel or with Israel to understand completely."
